slot.brief: Provide structures of three alkyl/benzyl halides in a figure; rank their rates of solvolysis (SN1) and justify via carbocation stability.

stem: The compounds shown in the figure undergo solvolysis under identical conditions. What is their rate order by the $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism?

verdicts.working: SN1 rate follows benzylic carbocation stability. The para-methoxy group stabilizes it by resonance, while para-nitro destabilizes it; therefore (iii) > (ii) > (i).

SN1 rate depends on stability of the benzylic carbocation. (iii) p-methoxybenzyl chloride: OMe donates by resonance (+M), strongly stabilizing the cation → fastest. (ii) benzyl chloride: unsubstituted reference. (i) p-nitrobenzyl chloride: NO2 withdraws by -M/-I, destabilizing the cation → slowest. Order: (iii) > (ii) > (i).

working:
Ionization gives benzylic carbocations; the rate-determining step is C–Cl bond cleavage.
The $p$-methoxy group stabilizes the benzylic cation by resonance donation.
The unsubstituted benzyl cation is intermediate in stability.
The $p$-nitro group withdraws electron density and destabilizes the cation.
Rate order: (i) > (ii) > (iii).
solution: In an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction, the rate-determining C–Cl bond cleavage forms a benzylic carbocation. The $p$-methoxy group stabilizes it by resonance, while the $p$-nitro group destabilizes it; hence the rate order is $(i)>(ii)>(iii)$.

For (i), draw a benzene ring with a –CH2Cl group and a –OCH3 group at para positions. For (ii), draw a benzene ring with only a –CH2Cl group. For (iii), draw a benzene ring with a –CH2Cl group and a –NO2 group at para positions. Show the substituent bonds and labels clearly; include no arrows or other text.
